messages:
Maria: Heads up — I’m planning to land PR #18290 but I’m going to hold it for now because of the nightly deploy freeze at 23:00 UTC. Can someone check CI and whether we can squeeze this into the 21:30 canary window? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pull/18290

Alex: @Maria running the matrix now. mac-e2e is failing consistently. Quick snippet of the failure: 
```
TimeoutError: failed to connect to localstack on attempt 3
at tests/integration/localstack_helper.rb:42
```
I’ll kick a rerun.

CI Bot: Build #5489 (PR 18290) queued on ubuntu-22.04, macos-11, windows-2022

Sam: Note — main had the schema migration merged yesterday, so this PR will need a rebase. Rebase + CI typically ~10–20m if no flake. If mac keeps failing that adds time.

Maria: Understood. Is there a hard cutoff for canary start? @Release Captain

Release Captain: Cutoff for canary start is 21:15 UTC so the canary can finish before the 23:00 freeze window. If the rebase + rerun path looks >30m total, better to defer to tomorrow. Don’t risk a rollback.

Alex: Rerun finished — mac-e2e still failing, different error this time (network-related). Full log uploaded to PR.

Jordan: I can take a look at the mac flake in ~15m. If it’s a flaky infra thing I can workaround the test quickly. @Sam any gotchas with schema changes I should know about?

Sam: Thanks, Jordan. Main changed the DB index name; tests need the new fixture ordering. If you can patch that in a tiny commit I’ll rebase and land. Otherwise we should hold.

Jordan: Sounds good — I’ll open a tiny test-fix commit and drop a note in the PR.

Maria: I’m putting the PR on hold for now to avoid risking the freeze. Will add label and update release notes.

Maria: PR comment added: "Hold: waiting on mac-e2e flake fix and small test update; will re-open for merge tomorrow AM if green" :thumbsup:

CI Bot: PR 18290 labeled do-not-merge/hold by Maria

Alex: Thanks all — ping me if Jordan’s patch lands and you want me to handle the rebase+final smoke run.

Maria: Appreciated. Closing this loop — we’ll target a morning canary when we have time to iterate.
